intent: Trainer CronJob, train command with Lease, and Helm chart
Lease lock, train command, Helm chart and chart checks

title: the chart renders the trainer and reusable pod-template helpers, not the application Deployment
why: Injection into workloads belongs to the team's own chart (or warden), and rendering a Deployment would duplicate and drift from it. Named templates taking the values map let a parent chart include the same fetch init container the trainer is rendered from, so both describe the launch identically.
alternative: Also render the Deployment — rejected: duplicates the team's spec

title: coordinate trainers with a Kubernetes Lease through a dependency-free API client
why: Create is atomic, an unrenewed lease expires so a crashed trainer cannot block training, and takeover carries the resourceVersion so one taker wins. Four REST calls with the JDK HTTP client avoid a large client-library tree, consistent with the OCI client decision.
alternative: No lock — rejected: ADR 0002 chose the Lease after review

title: train reports every outcome and exits 0; usage errors exit 2; --strict exits 1 on failure
why: The trainer is a CronJob, not on the pod start path, so a failed run only needs to be visible and retried by the schedule; a misconfigured command line should still fail visibly.
alternative: Exit non-zero on failure — rejected by ADR 0002: failures are logged and retried

name: KubernetesLeaseLock
role: TrainingLock on a Lease named mnemo-warmup-<fingerprint hex>; renews in the background; deletes on close only if still the holder
conditions: Needs get/create/update/delete on leases in its namespace; expiry compares renewTime plus leaseDurationSeconds on the local clock

name: TrainingOrchestrator
role: Decides ALREADY_STORED, LOCKED_BY_OTHER, TRAINED or FAILED in the order check, lock, re-check, train, upload, release
conditions: Never throws; does not publish if the lock was lost

name: Helm chart
role: Trainer CronJob, RBAC and named templates for the fetch init container, volumes, env and entrypoint
conditions: Templates take the values map; app.image/jar/jvmArgs/env must match the Deployment

subject: JDK HttpClient and plain http
why: On http:// it tries an h2c upgrade, which kubectl proxy answers with a 500 even though the object was created; found only against a real API server, so the client is pinned to HTTP/1.1

subject: Image-pull secrets
why: Only the kubelet sees them, so the registry credentials for fetch and the trainer are mounted as separate dockerconfigjson Secrets

subject: cp -a as non-root
why: It prints ownership errors on an emptyDir; cp -R keeps the executable bits and is silent

intent: Address review: lease ownership expiry, repair of broken entries

title: report lease ownership lost two thirds of the duration after the last successful renewal
why: Swallowing every API error left held() true forever, so a partitioned trainer could publish after its lease expired and another trainer took over. A monotonic trust window of two missed renewals makes it stop claiming the lease well before expiry; only definite answers (deleted, other holder, conflict) lose it permanently.
alternative: Treat any API error as a loss — rejected: a brief outage would abort healthy training

title: inspect an entry's completeness and replace broken ones instead of trusting the tag
why: exists() only saw the manifest tag, so a tag with a missing blob made every run report ALREADY_STORED and nothing repaired it. inspect checks the manifest, the config blob and the archive blob's size without downloading the archive; put already re-uploads missing blobs and rewrites the tag.
alternative: Download and fully verify the archive each run — rejected: hundreds of MB every schedule interval

subject: A lease is advisory
why: A lost lease during upload can still lead to two publishers; harmless because each entry is a digest-verified pair written by one atomic tag update, and the outcome says so

subject: Tag immutability
why: Replacing a broken entry rewrites the tag, so a registry with immutable tags refuses it and the run reports FAILED

subject: Same-length archive damage
why: inspect cannot see it without downloading; fetch verifies the bytes before use
